To promote self-reliance, education and wellbeing of orphaned and vulnerable children, women and youth in the informal settlements.
To see a community free from illiteracy, lack of sustainable income and poor health.
Provide food, shelter and education for orphaned and vulnerable children.

Offer training in hygiene, environmental management, and skills and technical training.
Offer counselling, medical referral, and food and nutrition support.

Promote awareness of preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission, and maternal, newborn and child health among young women.
Encourage exchange between Smile and local, national and international organisations to build capacity and share ideas and culture.

Margret Nekesa serving the children at Smile
That her smile combined with other aspects of life can change the world.
What Margret believes, and what every day at Smile is built on.
The eldest daughter, sent with her sisters to their grandfather's farm, where she struggled to stay in school.
A severe spinal condition kept her in one room, caring for three children. She prayed to walk again so she could help others.
She began serving her community, enrolling children in school and sharing her own home with those who had nowhere to go.
She registered the Smile self-help group, training women and youth and feeding street children.
Smile was registered as a Community Based Organisation.
Supported by her three children and friends of Smile, the centre keeps growing in Soweto, Kayole.
